summary.one_liner: A framework of software engineering career ladders (Developer, Tech Lead, Technical Program Manager, Engineering Manager) that managers can use to guide career-growth conversations with their reports.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a career-ladder framework for software engineering managers to discuss expectations for each position and plan next steps. It defines four ladders: Developer, Tech Lead, Technical Program Manager, and Engineering Manager, across levels 1 to 7, with Senior starting at level 4. Each position is rated on five axes (Technology, System, People, Process, Influence), and each axis has five cumulative levels, such as Adopts/Specializes/Evangelizes/Masters/Creates for Technology. The Influence axis is treated as orthogonal and applies across the other axes. The README also includes FAQs on using the framework, collecting evidence, and promotion timing, plus links to other pages covering each position. It is presented as a baseline to adapt, not a strict checklist.
use_cases: Preparing career-growth conversations with direct reports
Defining expectations for each engineering level
Comparing Tech Lead and Engineering Manager roles
Adapting a career ladder for a company's own engineering levels
notable: Uses radar charts with five axes (Technology, System, People, Process, Influence) to visualize a role's expectations
Influence is treated as a separate orthogonal dimension that applies to all other axes
Each axis has five cumulative performance levels, with each level including the previous ones
Covers four ladders with levels 1 to 7 in a single comparison table
Stops at level 7 by design and explains why
caveats: Explicitly not a checklist for promotion; the README says companies vary and examples of behavior are left for each team to write
Level 8 and above are not covered
The README does not describe any software or tooling; the links to individual position pages are listed but their content is not included here
